questions.question: 1. Are findings grouped because they share WORDS rather than root causes?
questions.verdict: MIXED - NO at the finding level, YES at the chapter level, and the chapter-level failure is confined to CH-F and CH-G.
questions.evidence: POSITIVE FIRST, because the absence matters: Agent A's method explicitly rejects 'same screen', 'shared words in the title', 'same wave', 'frontend vs backend', 'same technology' and 'same register domain letter', and it demonstrably applied that. Sixteen findings changed system against their recorded domain census, each with a stated mechanism: F058 ('avatars missing in chat' - an identity word) moved to RS-09 Governed Delivery because the browser reads the bucket directly and no identity change can fix it; F121 ('Articles images 404') moved to RS-08 Retention Truth because a resolved expiring URL was stored as if it were a reference; F071 ('a native call bug') moved to RS-21 Distribution because the shared code already carries both fixes and only the released binaries are stale; F035 ('an attention defect') moved to RS-02 because presentation cannot manufacture a media-connected fact; F124 ('a composer bug') moved to RS-04 because an ellipsis sentinel is transmitted as the message body. CH-F holds 33 findings spanning SEVEN root systems (RS-07..RS-13) and TEN deficiency classes (MISSING_AUTHORITY, DATA_MODEL_DEFICIENCY, ARCHITECTURE_CONTRADICTION, INCOMPLETE_IMPLEMENTATION, FRAGMENTED_AUTHORITY, LEGACY_COMPATIBILITY_DEBT, PRESENTATION_DEFICIENCY, VALIDATION_CERTIFICATION_DEBT, SHARED_DEFICIENCY_MANIFESTATION, OTHER_EVIDENCED). Its unifying token is 'content/media'; its unifying structure is a dependency CHAIN, which is a sequencing relation BETWEEN systems and therefore evidence that there are several.
